frameworkName: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook — Third-Party Relationships
licenseNote: Public domain (U.S. federal banking regulator publication). Summaries below are original, written for this application - not reproductions of FFIEC handbook text.
demonstrationSubsetDisclaimer: This is an illustrative subset for portfolio demonstration purposes, not full framework coverage.

controls.title: Third-party risk management program governance
controls.summary: The bank maintains a board-approved TPRM program with defined roles, risk appetite, and escalation paths for third-party relationships.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for evidence the program is bank-owned (board/committee approved), not solely a vendor attestation.

controls.title: Risk-based due diligence prior to contracting
controls.summary: Due diligence depth is scaled to the criticality of the service being outsourced (critical activities receive enhanced scrutiny).
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm the vendor's own documentation shows differentiated review depth by engagement type, not a one-size-fits-all checklist.

controls.title: Contractual risk allocation
controls.summary: Contracts define performance standards, audit rights, data ownership, liability allocation, and termination/exit terms.
controls.validationGuidance: Exit/termination terms are the most commonly missing element - check specifically for a defined transition-out obligation.

controls.title: Ongoing monitoring of critical third parties
controls.summary: Critical third parties are monitored on an ongoing basis, not only at onboarding, including periodic reassessment of financial condition and control effectiveness.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a defined monitoring cadence tied to criticality tier.

controls.title: Subcontractor (fourth-party) oversight
controls.summary: The vendor discloses and the bank has visibility into subcontractors performing critical functions on the bank's behalf.
controls.validationGuidance: Overlaps with NIST 800-161 C-SCRM-4; FFIEC additionally expects the bank to assess whether subcontracting was contractually pre-approved.

controls.title: Business continuity and incident response coordination
controls.summary: The vendor's continuity and incident response plans are coordinated with the bank's own plans, with defined communication protocols.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for evidence of a joint or coordinated tabletop exercise, not two independently-tested but disconnected plans.

controls.title: Data security and confidentiality controls
controls.summary: The vendor implements controls appropriate to the sensitivity of bank and customer data it processes.
controls.validationGuidance: Cross-reference against GLBA Safeguards Rule findings - this control and GLBA-1 through GLBA-3 often share the same evidence.

controls.title: Access control and authentication for bank systems
controls.summary: Vendor personnel accessing bank systems are subject to least-privilege access and strong authentication.
controls.validationGuidance: MFA enforcement for any vendor-side administrative access is a frequent examiner focus area.

controls.title: Foreign-based third-party risk considerations
controls.summary: Where a vendor operates or processes data outside the U.S., country-specific legal and operational risks are assessed.
controls.validationGuidance: Not applicable for a purely domestic vendor - mark NOT_APPLICABLE with justification rather than treating as a gap.

controls.title: Concentration risk assessment
controls.summary: The bank assesses risk from reliance on a single vendor across multiple critical functions, or from many banks relying on the same vendor sector-wide.
controls.validationGuidance: This is a portfolio-level control, not evaluable from a single vendor's evidence alone - typically validated at the dashboard/portfolio level, not per-vendor.

controls.title: Vendor financial condition monitoring
controls.summary: The bank monitors the ongoing financial viability of critical vendors to anticipate service disruption risk.
controls.validationGuidance: Evidence type here is atypical (financial statements/D&B reports rather than security documents) - flag for procurement/finance team review rather than security review.

controls.title: Examiner-ready documentation trail
controls.summary: TPRM decisions, risk acceptances, and monitoring results are documented in a form retrievable for regulatory examination.
controls.validationGuidance: This is effectively validated by the platform's own audit log and immutable review-decision records, not vendor-supplied evidence.
